newsitem.title: GERMANY: DAX trading seen skittish ahead of jobs, rate data.
newsitem.headline: DAX trading seen skittish ahead of jobs, rate data.

text.p: German shares were seen remaining weak on Monday afternoon and later into the week as traders watched cautiously for Bonn's unemployment figures on and interest rate developments in the U.S.

At 1445 GMT, the IBIS DAX index, which reflects all-day computer trading in the DAX, traded down 43.73 points at 4,292.72, while the DAX ended bourse trading down 111.85 points at 4,296.94, its first close below 4,300 since July 22.
"The market is very nervous right now," said one trader. "We're watching to see what happens to U.S. interest rates and what happens with unemployment in Germany."

After little new data arrived on Monday to boost trading, traders were looking ahead to Wednesday's announcement of July unemployment data. In June seasonally adjusted joblessness rose by 11,000 to 4.374 million.
"A drop would help private consumption," a trader said.
Shares could get a lift on Tuesday if a special session of parliament shows signs of a break-through on tax reform, traders said.
But another deadlock between the coalition and opposition Social Democrats would have little negative effect since most traders have already given up hope for tax cuts, they said.

Among individual shares, software group SAP AG was set to announce details of a venture with chip maker Intel Corp. at 1700 GMT on Tuesady. SAP shares closed floor trading on Monday down 7.50 marks at 424, and were down three at 425 in the afternoon IBIS sesssion.
Utility Veba AG, construction group Hochtief AG, athletic shoe maker Adidas AG and drug maker Schering AG planned to release mid-year results later this week.
In Monday afternoon IBIS trade, volumes were heaviest in banks stocks.
Deutsche Bank AG traded down 4.75 marks to 117.40, Commerzbank AG fell 1.15 to 61.50, and Dresdner Bank AG fell 3.40 to 80.50.
Bayerische Hypo-Bank, soon to merge with fellow Bavarian bank Vereinsbank was among the chief losers in floor trade,down 3.90 marks at 72.05 marks.

Chemical giant BASF AG was down 25 pfennigs at 70.40 marks and Bayer AG was down 95 pfennig 75.55 marks, while Schering was down 2.20 marks at 200.50 marks. Airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG was down 1.55 at 34.75 marks.
Some support came from the dollar's strength at 1.87 marks.
